content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% for high-sentiment periods.
- After a price spike (e.g., >48.0), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is negative (avg < -0.3) over last 5 days, model overconfidently forecasts upward; reduce forecast by 1–2% for each negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >47.0 for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward adjustment of 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after forecast peak, model fails to anticipate downward momentum; add a “reversal buffer” of 1–2% below forecast peak for 2–4 days post-peak.
- Sentiment history with repeated negative values (e.g., -0.5 or lower) correlates with underperformance; if sentiment is negative for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 5 days.
